parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, documented police/border targeting, facility ban, or organised violence; same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2022 and Pride, bars and youth tolerance indicate documented social acceptance. Residual risk comes from thin traveller recourse—no gender-identity anti-discrimination protection, LGBTI organisations cannot register, stigmatising media code—and undocumented border/document practice, plus resident healthcare/employment/school discrimination as climate signals. Functioning institutions and no recorded prison assaults mitigate, but do not create explicit protections.

entry_documents.exposure: No sourced account of how immigration officers treat document/presentation mismatch; status unresolved, not evidence of safety.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2022; no documented traveller-facing entry ban.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident surgical gatekeeping for legal gender recognition does not govern foreign passports; border practice is the unanswered interaction.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Section 294 obscene acts, up to 3 months, is a latent public-order lever; cited soliciting prosecutions are 1990-1994 and not disaggregated by gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison service reported 10 transgender inmates with no recorded assaults; no documented trans-specific detention practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention for public conduct could theoretically follow outing, but no documented current enforcement against trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access ban documented; gender-neutral toilets at two university colleges and one temporary conference conversion drew boycott/petition backlash.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender-neutral provision exists and community groups defend it as complementary; Pride and gay bars/clubs operate openly.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Venue-level provision coexists with public backlash; no national bathroom restriction is documented.

care_services.exposure: February 2025 stakeholder report documents discrimination/harassment in healthcare for trans residents and prohibitive surgical costs for recognition.
care_services.protection: Health minister in 2020 stated doctors should respect preferences including sexual orientation, with medical-council complaints.
care_services.interaction: Resident discrimination is a climate signal for visitor care; no documented visitor denial or medication-seizure practice.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Media regulator limits promotion/glamorisation of homosexuality; July 2025 broadcast code grouped homosexuality with paedophilia/incest, prompting review calls.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No trans-specific criminal offence; repeal of Section 377A in 2022 and community reports of feeling safer.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Stigmatising broadcast framing is sexuality-focused and latent, without documented police enforcement against trans presentation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Stakeholder report documents discrimination, abuse and restrictions for transgender students (residents); no documented visitor/minor school or custody rule.
minors_guardians.protection: No partner/family recognition for same-sex relationships; not documented as a traveller-facing restriction.
minors_guardians.interaction: A short-stay minor is not shown to enter resident schooling; exposure remains uncertain rather than documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data located, so no comparison with general homicide is possible; absence is not safety evidence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Annual Pride since 2009 drawing about 28,000, operating gay bars/clubs, and 2021 youth survey showing 80% willing to work with LGBTQ people indicate acceptance.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Backlash to a gender-neutral toilet shows segment hostility, while large Pride and operator guidance show a thriving social scene.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Workplace fairness law effective January 2025 omits gender identity/expression; LGBTI organisations cannot register; composite index values not extractable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Medical-council complaint route exists; no LGBTQ complaints in prior three years as of 2020, of limited current weight.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal recourse is thin for gender identity despite functioning state institutions; immigration treatment and governing basis for registration refusal remain unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that protections and acceptance coexist with discretionary friction and uncertainty, but this case lacks documented border stops, detention, or complaint-driven remedies, so it sits higher than the documented incident-plus-remedy pattern.

Similar reduced-risk level: occasional delays/friction without custody or exclusion. This case has thinner explicit protections than the anchor, but also no documented traveller detention, offset by undocumented border practice.

Higher because that anchor has explicit equality law, chosen-name documents, training and independent oversight. This dossier has acceptance and decriminalisation but no gender-identity statutory protection or documented traveller-facing safeguards, so it sits materially below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is decriminalised and socially tolerant enough for Pride, bars and open community life, with no documented traveller-facing restriction, targeting, or custodial abuse. The main exposures are indirect: stigmatising media rules, no gender-identity employment protection, unregistrable organisations, healthcare discrimination for residents, and an unresolved border/document question. Section 294 is a dated, latent public-order lever, not a documented trans-specific campaign. Functioning institutions mitigate street risk, but thin formal recourse and unknown entry practice keep the score a step below jurisdictions with working explicit protections.
